results.bound: (1+\varepsilon)-approximation in O(n log^2 n / \varepsilon^2) cut queries
results.quote: Theorem 3.4. Let _G_=(_V,E_) be a weighted graph. There is a randomized algorithm that makes \(O(nlog^2n/\varepsilon^2)\) cut queries and returns a \((1+\varepsilon)\)-approximation to the densest subgraph of _G_.
Lemma 3.5. The randomized query complexity of a \((2-\delta)\)-approximation for DSG is \(\Omega(n/logn)\), for any \(\delta>0\).

results.bound: (1+\varepsilon)-approximation in O(n log^2 n / \varepsilon^2) cut queries
results.previous_best: O(n log^3 n (\log n + 1/\varepsilon^2)) queries by Plevrakis et al. [ICALP ’18]
results.quote: Corollary 3.6. Let _G_=(_V,E_) be a weighted graph. There is a randomized algorithm that makes \(O(nlog^2n/\varepsilon^2)\) cut queries and returns a \((1+\varepsilon)\)-approximation to the maximum cut of _G_.

results.bound: (1+\varepsilon)-approximation in O(n r log n / \varepsilon^2) cut and edge queries
results.quote: Theorem 3.7. Let _H_=(_V,E_) be a weighted hypergraph, with rank _r_ unknown. There is a randomized algorithm that makes \(O(nrlogn/\varepsilon^2)\) cut and edge queries and returns a \((1+\varepsilon)\)- approximation to the densest subhypergraph of _H_.

results.bound: No o(\sqrt{n}/(1+p^{-1}))-approximation with cut queries alone with probability at least p
results.quote: Theorem 4.1. With only cut access to a hypergraph, it is impossible to obtain an \(o(\sqrt{n}/(1+p^{-1}))\)-approximation for DSH with probability at least _p_.

results.bound: No approximation with cut queries alone with probability greater than 3/n
results.quote: Theorem 4.2. With only cut access to a hypergraph, it is impossible to obtain any approximation for D_kSH with probability greater than 3_/n_.

results.bound: No approximation with edge queries making t queries with probability greater than (1+2t)/2^{n/2}
results.quote: Theorem 4.3. With only edge access to a hypergraph, it is impossible for an algorithm making _t_ queries to obtain any approximation for D_kSH with probability greater than \(\frac{1+2t}{2^{n/2}}\).

results.bound: Deterministic cut query complexity at least \binom{n}{r}
results.quote: Theorem 5.1. The deterministic cut query complexity of D_kSH on rank-_r_ hypergraphs is at least \(\genfrac(){pt}{2}{n}{r}\), for any \(r\le k\le n-r\).
Corollary 5.3. The deterministic query complexity of D_kS on weighted graphs is at least \(\genfrac(){pt}{2}{n}{2}\), for any \(2\le k\le n-2\).
Lemma 5.4. The randomized query complexity of a \((1.5-\delta)\)-approximation for D_kS on unweighted graphs is \(\Omega(n^2/logn)\), for any \(\delta>0\).

Theorem 5.5. The randomized query complexity of D_kSH on rank-_r_ hypergraphs is at least \(\Omega(n\genfrac(){pt}{2}{n/2}{\lfloor(2r-1)/3\rfloor}/(r^2logn))\), for any combination of cut, add, and edge queries. If _r=O_(1), this yields a lower bound of \(\Omega(n^{\lfloor(2r+2)/3\rfloor}/logn)\) queries.

results.bound: \Omega\left(\binom{n}{r-1} / (n^2 r \log n)\right) queries for a (1+1/(r+1)-\delta)-approximation; if r=O(1), \Omega(n^{r-3}/\log n)
results.quote: Theorem 5.6. The randomized query complexity of a \((1+1/(r+1)-\delta)\)-approximation of D_kSH on rank-_r_ hypergraphs is at least \(\Omega(\genfrac(){pt}{2}{n}{r-1}/(n^2rlogn))\), for any \(\delta>0\) and any combination of cut, add, and edge queries. If _r=O_(1), this yields a lower bound of \(\Omega(n^{r-3}/logn)\) queries.
Theorem 5.7. The randomized query complexity of D_kSH on rank-_r_ hypergraphs where _r=O_(1) is \(\Omega(n^{max\{r-3,\lfloor(2r+2)/3\rfloor\}}/logn)\).

results.bound: With cut and is-edge queries, approximating add(S) with probability greater than 1/2 + 2t/2^{n/5} is impossible
results.quote: Theorem 6.1. With only cut and is-edge<sup>?</sup> access to a hypergraph, there exists a hypergraph _H_ with a node subset _S_ such that it is impossible for an algorithm making _t_ queries to obtain any approximation to add(_S_) with probability greater than \(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{2t}{2^{n/5}}\).

Proposition 1. Let _G_=(_V,E_) be a weighted graph. There is a deterministic algorithm that makes \(O(n/\varepsilon)\mathtt{cut}\) queries and returns a \((2+\varepsilon)\)-approximation to the densest subgraph of _G_.
